questions.question: A sum of Rs. 3000 becomes Rs. 4320 in 2 years at a certain rate of compound interest (compounding annually). How much this sum will become after 4 years?

A = P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ

questions.question: The length of a cuboid is 4 cm. If the breadth of the cuboid is four times of its length and height of the cuboid is twice of its length, then what is the lateral surface area of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Length** ($L$) = 4 cm; **Breadth** ($B$) = 4 × 4 = 16 cm; **Height** ($H$) = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

**Lateral Surface Area** = 2 × $H$ × ($L$ + $B$)

**Lateral Surface Area** = 2 × 8 × (4 + 16) = 16 × 20 = 320 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 320 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of cuboid ($L$) = 4 cm

**Breadth** of cuboid ($B$) = 4 × $L$ = 4 × 4 = 16 cm

**Height** of cuboid ($H$) = 2 × $L$ = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Lateral Surface Area** of cuboid = 2 × $H$ × ($L$ + $B$)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6aac2b2d29c74e2e758f2af46a977b5dcedb49e005a2f9897b7de7f2f5a07499.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Lateral Surface Area** = 2 × 8 × (4 + 16)

⇒ **Lateral Surface Area** = 16 × 20

⇒ **Lateral Surface Area** = 320 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 320 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The total surface area includes all six faces and is calculated as TSA = 2($LB$ + $BH$ + $HL$).

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is given by the product of its dimensions: Volume = $L$ × $B$ × $H$.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal: Diagonal = √($L$² + $B$² + $H$²).</p

questions.question:
Two Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All sparrows are birds.

Some owls are birds.

**Conclusions:**

I. No sparrow is an owl.

II. Some sparrows are owls.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a2b222b541484358e565f6fc0eb6cb4a10eb806dcabc4e39e88ab43aa46e01b.png] 

Conclusions:

I. No sparrow is an owl → Does not Follow (As, all sparrows are birds and some owls are birds. So, as no direct negative or cross relation is given between sparrow and owls therefore, it is definitely false)

II. Some sparrows are owls → Does not Follow (As, all sparrows are birds and some owls are birds. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here,

 
• Elements i.e sparrow and owl are same in both the conclusions.
 
• Both the conclusions are individually does not follow(possible but not definitely true).
 
• Conclusion I and II are complementary pair i.e Some and No

Hence, the correct answer is "Either conclusion I or II follows".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• The elements should be same in both the conclusions
 
• Both conclusions should possible but not definitely true.
 
• One of the conclusion should be negative and one of the conclusion should be positive i.e complimentary pair.
 
• Complimentary pairs :

 
• ​some + no and all + some not

questions.question:
Public goods possess which of the following features in the economy?

I. They are non-rivalrous.

II. They are non-excludable.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Public goods are goods or services that are consumed by everyone in the society, regardless of whether they have paid for it or not.
 
• **Non-rivalrous means that one person's consumption of the good does not reduce the amount available for others.**
 
• For example, if a park is a **public good,** one person's enjoyment of the park does not prevent others from enjoying it as well.
 
• **Non-excludable means that it is difficult or impossible to prevent someone from consuming the good, even if they have not paid for it.**
 
• For example, it is difficult to prevent someone from enjoying the view of a fireworks display from a public space, even if they have not paid for a ticket to attend the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Private goods are goods or services that are consumed by individuals who have paid for them.
 
• **Private goods** **are both** **rivalrous and excludable.**
 
• **Common goods are goods or services that are available to everyone in the society but are rivalrous.**
 
• For example,** fish in a lake **can be a common good because if one person catches a fish, there is one less fish available for others to catch.
 
• **Club goods are goods or services that are non-rivalrous but excludable.**
 
• For example, a subscription to a streaming service is a club good because multiple people can consume the service at the same time without reducing the amount available for others, but only those who have paid for the subscription can access it.
